review_text: The temple grounds were remarkably peaceful early in the morning and public cleanliness was spotless. However, the afternoon crowd at the bamboo grove was overwhelming.
Incredible culinary experience with authentic kaiseki dinners. The subway was straightforward and felt very safe walking back to our hotel at midnight.
Bus transport was heavily congested and buses were too crowded to board during peak hours. Prices near the station were also somewhat expensive.
The historic cathedral architecture is breathtaking and the Uffizi art collection is magnificent. Watch out for pickpockets near the central train station.
Exceptional pasta and gelato at reasonable prices in the residential quarter. The hotel accommodation was clean and the host was very friendly.
Endless queues and chaotic crowds under the summer sun ruined the visit to the main square. Exorbitant ticket fees for basic museums.
Pristine mountain scenery and turquoise glacial lakes that took our breath away. Hiking trails were clean, well marked, and we felt completely safe.
Hotel accommodations were overpriced and restaurant meals were expensive throughout the park town. The shuttle bus transport was punctual though.
Peaceful nature escape with crisp mountain air. Staff at the visitor center were polite and helpful with wildlife safety advice.
Spectacular sunset views over the caldera and whitewashed buildings. The local seafood dinner was delicious and fresh.
Extremely crowded alleys with tourists pushing for photos. Taxis were a complete rip-off with exorbitant rates and no meters.
Our cliffside hotel room had a comfortable bed and breathtaking view. Cleanliness was good although tap water is not drinkable.
Table mountain hike offered panoramic views of the entire ocean coast. Friendly hospitality from locals and wonderful vineyard tours.
Delicious dining at very affordable prices given the exchange rate. Certain neighborhoods require strict safety vigilance after dark.
Public transport outside the city center is limited so we had to rely on taxis. The waterfront area was spotless and vibrant.
World-class adventure sports with exhilarating jet boating and bungee jumps. Town was clean, safe, and surrounded by majestic alpine peaks.
Accommodations were difficult to book and pricey during high season. The lakefront cafes had great burgers and welcoming service.
Easy walking town with scenic trails right from downtown. Prices for guided activities are steep but worth every penny.
Incredible gastronomy with rich traditional moles and street food stalls. The colonial architecture was colorful and well preserved.
Very budget-friendly with cheap market meals and inexpensive handicrafts. Hotel staff treated us like family with outstanding hospitality.
Traffic noise was noticeable in the central district and sidewalks were narrow. Cleanliness in some market restrooms could be improved.
Walking along the medieval stone walls provides unforgettable views of the Adriatic Sea. The marble streets in the Old Town were spotless.
Massive cruise ship crowds made the pedestrian streets suffocating in the afternoon. Food prices inside the walls were an expensive tourist trap.
Safe atmosphere with no crime worries at all. Local bus transport from outside the old town was convenient and cheap.
Beautiful lush green rice terraces and serene Hindu water temples. Friendly locals who greeted us with warm smiles everywhere we traveled.
Severe traffic gridlock between tourist hubs took hours to navigate. Litter and plastic pollution along some public beaches was disappointing.
Great value luxury villas with private pools and spotless rooms. Delicious tropical fruits and cafe dining for just a few dollars.
Fairytale Gothic and Baroque architecture with the stunning Charles Bridge. Public trams and metro system are fast, punctual, and cheap.
Aggressive scam artists and money exchange rip-offs near the astronomical clock. The Old Town square was shoulder-to-shoulder with tour groups.
Tempting bakeries with warm trdelnik and great historic beer halls with hearty food. Clean streets and felt very safe walking around.
An awe-inspiring archaeological wonder when you emerge through the Siq to the Treasury. The sheer scale of the rock-carved tombs is unmatched.
Persistent touts and animal handlers hassling tourists for donkey rides. Very hot with limited shade and expensive water bottles inside.
The local Bedouin hospitality and mint tea was wonderful. Make sure to wear sturdy hiking shoes because the trail involves miles of walking.
Cleanest air and purest drinking water anywhere on earth. The geothermal baths were soothing and the coastal scenery was dramatic.
Everything is exceptionally expensive from a simple sandwich to rental cars. However, safety is practically 100% with zero street crime.
Compact walkable city with cozy cafes and colorful modern architecture. Public bus network was simple to use and always on time.
